method: Read-only source/formula crosscheck and alpha>=128 contour pixel bounds. No PNG mutation. Alpha bounds include accessories and are not semantic body-size evidence.

mathParity.explanation: Executed actual JS destinationRect/transformRect versus separately transcribed Swift center/frame/scale/offset arithmetic, not an execution of SwiftUI.

nativeScreenshotChromaMeasurement.method: RGB max-min>45, max>90, bounding box. Activity x>=260 excluded to avoid panel. Different from alpha bounds; not a runtime GeometryReader measurement.

guardrailFindings: All current main/candidate scales and durations satisfy stricter native limits. Web scale currently accepts any positive finite value while native allows 0.1...4; future normalized values need both checks.
The catalog master.scale is presently 1 and unused by both renderers. clip.scale is the effective per-clip field.

Frame-strip 144x144 thumbnails now use a shared 832x992 classic stage: factor=144/992 and horizontal centering, applied to actual destinationRect including clip.scale. They no longer fit each transparent N canvas; source regression checks verify the destination.
SwiftUI fits a stage into the OS safe GeometryReader and converts points to physical pixels through display scale. Do not equate a 416px-wide screenshot with a 416px-wide content stage.
Contour bounding boxes contain hats, pillows, dumbbells and bathtub. Semantic body landmarks are needed for costume-size consistency; equal stage or canvas is not proof.
The region anchor is a placement baseline, not necessarily anatomical feet. Space-charging and chef include seat cushions, so anchor-to-eye distance is not a valid eye-to-foot body measurement.
